hashGenerator.title: Hash Generator
hashGenerator.description: Generate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 hashes from text input using Web Crypto API. All processing happens locally in your browser.
hashGenerator.faq1a: A hash function maps input data to a fixed-size byte sequence. The same input always produces the same output, but even a tiny change in input produces a completely different hash.
hashGenerator.faq2a: SHA-256 is the general-purpose recommendation. SHA-1 and MD5 are provided for legacy compatibility but are considered insecure for cryptographic use. SHA-512 produces a longer hash and is useful for high-security contexts.
hashGenerator.faq3a: Currently this tool only supports text input. For file hashing, you can paste the file content as text, or use a command-line tool like sha256sum.

htmlPreview.title: HTML Preview
htmlPreview.description: Write HTML and see it rendered live in a sandboxed iframe. Great for prototyping, learning, and testing HTML/CSS snippets.
htmlPreview.placeholder:
Hello World

Edit this HTML and see the preview live!
htmlPreview.faq1a: Yes, the preview runs in a sandboxed iframe that restricts scripts, forms, and same-origin access for safety.
htmlPreview.faq2q: Can I use CSS and JavaScript in the preview?
htmlPreview.faq2a: Inline <style> and <script> tags inside the HTML are supported. External resource references via <link> or <script src> are blocked by the sandbox.
htmlPreview.faq3q: Why is my external resource not loading?
htmlPreview.faq3a: The sandbox restricts loading external resources for security. Embed all CSS and JS inline in your HTML for the best results.

cronExpression.title: Cron Expression Builder
cronExpression.description: Build cron expressions visually and get a human-readable explanation of what the schedule means.
cronExpression.faq1a: A cron expression is a string of 5 fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) that defines a recurring schedule. It is widely used in job schedulers on Unix-like systems.
cronExpression.faq2q: What does * mean in a cron field?
cronExpression.faq2a: An asterisk (*) means 'every possible value' for that field. For example, * in the hour field means 'every hour'.
cronExpression.faq3q: Can I use special characters like / and ,?
cronExpression.faq3a: Yes. Use / for step values (*/5 means every 5 units), , to list specific values (1,15 means both 1 and 15), and - for ranges (1-5 means 1 through 5). Currently the builder uses 'every' and 'specific' modes for common patterns.

cssUnitConverter.title: CSS Unit Converter
cssUnitConverter.description: Convert between px, rem, em, and % CSS units based on a configurable base font size (default 16px).
cssUnitConverter.faq1q: What is the default base font size?
cssUnitConverter.faq1a: The default base font size is 16px, which is the browser default. You can change it to match your project's root font size.
cssUnitConverter.faq2q: How are em and % different from rem?
cssUnitConverter.faq2a: rem is relative to the root element's font size, while em and % are relative to the parent element's font size. This tool assumes the same base for simplicity.
cssUnitConverter.faq3q: Why are my converted values different from other tools?
cssUnitConverter.faq3a: Conversion results depend on the base font size setting. Make sure this matches your project's root font-size (common values are 16px, 10px, or 14px).

stringCaseConverter.title: String Case Converter
stringCaseConverter.description: Convert text between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and PascalCase instantly.
stringCaseConverter.faq1a: camelCase starts with a lowercase letter and capitalizes the first letter of each subsequent word, e.g. myVariableName. It is common in JavaScript and Java.
stringCaseConverter.faq2a: snake_case uses underscores between words and is common in Python, Ruby, and database column names, e.g. my_variable_name.
stringCaseConverter.faq3q: How does the converter handle acronyms?
stringCaseConverter.faq3a: The converter splits words on common delimiters (spaces, underscores, hyphens) and handles consecutive uppercase letters as acronyms. For example, 'XMLParser' converts to 'xml_parser' in snake_case.

ipLookup.title: IP Lookup
ipLookup.description: Look up geolocation, ISP, and timezone information for any IPv4 address using the ipapi.co API.
ipLookup.error: Failed to look up IP address
ipLookup.invalidIp: Please enter a valid IPv4 address
ipLookup.faq1q: What information does IP Lookup provide?
ipLookup.faq1a: IP Lookup returns geolocation data (city, region, country, coordinates), network information (ISP, organization, ASN), and timezone for the given IPv4 address.
ipLookup.faq2q: Is my IP address stored or tracked?
ipLookup.faq2a: No. This tool sends the IP you enter directly to ipapi.co and does not store or log any queries.
ipLookup.faq3a: Lookups can fail if the IP address is invalid, reserved (e.g. 192.168.x.x), or if the ipapi.co API rate limit has been exceeded (1,000 requests/day for free tier).
